title: [Formatting prerequisite] Format existing Python files used by the Torch stack
body:
Format existing Python files before introducing the Torch feature stack.

## Standard information about the request

This is a: formatting and import-order cleanup.

This change affects: existing Python files used by the following feature PRs.

This change changes: source presentation; no dependencies are added. Structural and static checks are recorded below.

## Motivation

Separating baseline formatting gives each subsequent feature PR a diff focused on its runtime behavior and tests.

## Contents

Pinned Ruff 0.14.6 formatting in 83 existing Python files, using the repository configuration. I001 import ordering is limited to production modules; `test/**` and `setup.py` receive no new import-sorting changes. This includes whitespace, line wrapping, quotes, docstring layout and import ordering/packing in the selected modules. Six tests never reformatted by the feature stack are excluded. Import additions/removals and executable rewrites stay in the feature PRs; no Torch modules or compiled kernels are added here. The frame-reader and MKL baselines are also formatted here against the original CPU source. The shared CPU MKL descriptor-cache change is excluded from the Torch scope.

## Links to any issues or associated PRs

Starts directly from `torch-stack-base`. PR #20 is withdrawn from this stack.

Base: `torch-stack-base`. Head: `torch-formatting-base` at `2b547a271aed7e88132811c632f0a5b3d6ee77a7`.

Unchanged original CPU reference: `40e94792b3edf59f39b18b65102b28a4f74433a7`.

[Campaign and test evidence](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/tree/31039e44d35ece9c6d755bd265c854d2bd8bb6a6/original-cpu-restoration); [tested-source mapping and documentation checks](https://github.com/xangma/pycbc/tree/a5d237cb4f4ed7a4e26d6b8ffa4aa0c1fc7b2964/original-cpu-restoration/final-publication).

**Torch CPU and Torch CUDA: 1991 triggers each, FAIL** against both CPU controls under unchanged trigger/full-PSD gates. Only four recorded runtime/timing fields are excluded; raw and corrected verdicts are retained. No performance samples or speedup claim.
